title: US memo says Nvidia's Huang dated suspected Chinese spy
summary: Officials believe Alice Huang, an executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed, was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security, the Financial Times reports.
bullets:
- A US intelligence memo concluded that **Nvidia** CEO **Jensen Huang** had a romantic relationship with Megaspeed executive **Alice Huang**, according to the Financial Times.
- The New York Times The New York Times Company reported Friday that Beijing's top spy agency recruited her to gather intelligence on US AI chips and Nvidia.
- Nvidia declined to comment, and three Republican House committee chairs have asked Huang to attend a closed-door briefing on **Nov. 18**.

sections.heading: FT: US Memo Alleges Nvidia's Jensen Huang Had Romantic Tie to Suspected Chinese Spy
sections.body:
A US intelligence memo concluded that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at one of the chipmaker's Singapore customers, according to the Financial Times. US officials believe China's Ministry of State Security recruited her to gather information on the American company. Before Donald Trump traveled to Beijing in May, the memo was shared with a small group of senior US officials, NDTV Profit reported, citing the FT.

The report puts the head of the world's most important AI chipmaker, who is also an influential ally of Trump, at the center of a counterintelligence inquiry. It comes as Washington continues to argue over which advanced chips should be allowed to reach China.

sections.heading: What the Memo Alleges
sections.body:
The FT report came one day after The New York Times reported on Friday, November 6, that Alice Huang, whose Chinese name is Huang Le, was recruited to collect intelligence on Jensen Huang. According to the Times, Beijing wanted to learn more about US AI chips and possibly push Nvidia to make its most advanced chips available to China. Officials drafted the memo earlier this year based on intelligence agency information, Chosun Ilbo reported.

Alice Huang was a senior executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that builds data centers in Southeast Asia using Nvidia chips and rents computing power to Chinese firms such as Alibaba, according to Chosun. US authorities have been examining whether chips were smuggled into China since late 2024. Investigators reportedly found her close relationship with Jensen Huang while they were monitoring her as part of that inquiry.

sections.heading: Nvidia's Response
sections.body:
Nvidia declined to comment on the memo or on the alleged romantic relationship. The White House and CIA also declined to comment, per NDTV Profit. Earlier, the company had called the two executives' contacts routine customer relations and said its internal investigation found no evidence of chip smuggling. "Meeting with customers is part of the CEO's job, and Jensen speaks with thousands of client executives annually," the company said, as quoted by Chosun. Megaspeed said it had opened its own investigation and would cooperate with US authorities. On October 30, China's foreign ministry dismissed the allegations as a "smear campaign."

Trump said he did not know about the specific intelligence concerns but hoped Huang would be cleared, The Economic Times reported.

sections.heading: Congress Seeks a Briefing
sections.body: Three Republican House committee chairs, Brian Mast, John Moolenaar and Rick Crawford, have asked Huang to attend a closed-door briefing on November 18. They want to hear about his interactions with Alice Huang and how Nvidia protects itself against foreign espionage, and they asked him to respond by November 11, NDTV Profit reported. In a statement, the House Select Committee on China described Alice Huang as "a publicly reported Chinese intelligence asset," Bloomberg reported.

title: PSI says Anthropic-powered AI proved quantum conjecture
summary: The startup says its system cracked a problem open since 2008, with the Lean proof assistant verifying it; peer review remains pending.
bullets:
- **Physical Superintelligence** said Friday its research system, using an unreleased **Anthropic** model, proved the **Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture** on day three of a run.
- The result means quantum computers gain at most polynomial speedups on random inputs, measured by input queries rather than total computing time.
- **Stanford** researchers called it "a huge result," though journal peer review is pending and PSI hasn't named the Anthropic model it used.

sections.heading: PSI says AI system running unreleased Anthropic model proved Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture
sections.body: Physical Superintelligence (PSI), a physics-focused AI startup, said on Friday, Nov. 6, that a research system it built proved the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, a quantum complexity problem open since 2008, using instances of a non-public Anthropic model. The company said the system had a complete proof on the third day of a run on its own infrastructure, and the Lean proof assistant accepted it. The result has not yet passed journal peer review. For now it is a company claim, but the paper and the machine-checked proof are public, so outside experts can test it.

sections.heading: What the proof claims
sections.body:
The conjecture asks whether quantum computers can be exponentially faster than ordinary ones on random inputs, which almost never contain the hidden patterns that algorithms like Shor's factoring method exploit. Aaronson and Ambainis showed that if their statement about bounded low-degree polynomials held, quantum speedups on random inputs would be at most polynomial. PSI's announcement framed the result this way: "a quantum computer cannot save exponentially many looks unless the string has a rare pattern". The theorem limits how many times an algorithm reads its input, not total computing time, which leaves room for practical quantum advantages.

The first proof gave a weaker bound. After PSI set the system on related open problems, it improved the result twice, and Lean accepted the final version. The argument follows a plan by Shachar Lovett and Jiapeng Zhang. It replaces an inequality they had left as a conjecture with a new one, proved by pairing input settings through a determinant.

sections.heading: Human roles and checks
sections.body:
PSI staff member David Turturean built and ran the system, prompted the model to draft the paper, and is responsible for its correctness. Advisers Jim Halverson and Phiala Shanahan audited the proof and commented on the formalization. The project's GitHub repository says the proof, paper and formalization were produced by AI models. It also says the Lean theorems contain no placeholders or added axioms and were re-checked by two independent kernel implementations. Readers still need to confirm that the formal statement matches the original conjecture.

Stanford researchers Guy Blanc, Jordan Docter, Carmen Strassle and Li-Yang Tan settled a special case in August. They have been reading the full proof and, in a statement published by PSI, called it "a huge result" in which "everything is brought together in a rather magical way".

sections.heading: Unanswered questions
sections.body: PSI has not said which Anthropic model it used, and Anthropic did not respond to a request for comment. The announcement follows OpenAI's September claim that it had solved a problem involving the Navier-Stokes equations, and it adds to a debate over what AI means for mathematicians' careers.

title: Ex-OpenAI engineer pleads not guilty to bugging office
summary: Abdulrahman Alfozan is accused of hiding a recording device at OpenAI's San Francisco headquarters, as reports detail years of internal security warnings.
bullets:
- Former **OpenAI** engineer **Abdulrahman Alfozan** pleaded not guilty Friday in San Francisco to a federal charge of intercepting oral communications, Courthouse News reported.
- Prosecutors allege he hid a toilet-paper-wrapped recorder behind a conference room TV; he faces up to five years in prison if convicted.
- Reuters Thomson Reuters Corporation reported staff warned of security lapses for years; OpenAI says its sensitive work is kept in restricted repositories.

sections.heading: OpenAI bugging suspect Alfozan pleads not guilty as security lapses reported
sections.body: Abdulrahman Alfozan, the former OpenAI engineer accused of hiding a listening device in an executive conference room at the company's San Francisco headquarters, pleaded not guilty in federal court on Friday, November 6, according to CNBC. The plea comes days after Reuters reported that OpenAI employees had warned leadership and the board about weak internal security for years, starting before ChatGPT launched in late 2022.

sections.heading: The court hearing
sections.body:
Alfozan's lawyer, David Rizk, entered the plea before Magistrate Judge Peter H. Kang, Bloomberg reported. A grand jury indicted the 35-year-old Saudi national on Oct. 27 on one count of intercepting oral communications. If convicted, he faces up to five years in prison, a $250,000 fine and possible deportation, according to Courthouse News. Alfozan, a U.S. permanent resident, worked at OpenAI from July 2025 until the FBI arrested him on Oct. 9 and the company fired him. His next court date is set for Nov. 17.

Prosecutors say Alfozan wrapped a recording device in toilet paper and hid it behind a television in a conference room. They also say his wife's chatbot history showed several prompts about building, testing and hiding an audio recorder, Business Insider reported. At an earlier hearing, a judge called him a flight risk and denied bond. A court filing also says he used an internal OpenAI AI tool to look up executives' trips to Saudi Arabia, and that he was in regular contact with a Saudi royal who tried to recruit him for a new AI venture there, Reuters reported.

sections.heading: Years of internal warnings
sections.body:
Five people familiar with the matter told Reuters that some staff came to believe management cared more about keeping pace with Google and Anthropic than about security. One concern was that OpenAI kept most of its code in a single "monorepo," so anyone with code access could see details of sensitive projects unrelated to their own work, Reuters reported. Three people said internal tools, including the sandboxes researchers use to test new models, did not get regular security reviews.

OpenAI pushed back on parts of that account. The company said its most sensitive work sits in separate, restricted repositories and that the monorepo does not hold its model weights. It also said internal tools now get regular security reviews under security chief Dane Stuckey, The Next Web reported.

sections.heading: OpenAI's response
sections.body:
Two people told Reuters that executive Thibault Sottiaux has taken over an effort to secure OpenAI's internal systems. In August, he moved a quarter of the company's production engineers to security infrastructure work, according to Reuters reporting republished by The Economic Times. After Reuters asked for comment, OpenAI announced in a blog post that it was planning its "next internal security sprint."

"The actions we've taken recently show that program doing its job: identifying risks and responding decisively," OpenAI spokesperson Elana Widmann told Reuters.

title: El Niño turns very strong, WMO forecasts December peak
summary: WMO projects Pacific temperatures up to 3.8°C above average, while NOAA puts a 70% chance on the strongest event since 1950.
bullets:
- A **Meteored** analysis using **NOAA** criteria found that the warming in the central Pacific reached 2.0°C above normal for August through October, pushing El Niño into the "very strong" category.
- The **World Meteorological Organization** projects tropical Pacific waters may reach 3.8°C above average through January, with Secretary-General **Celeste Saulo** calling it "off the monitoring charts".
- A European model released Nov. 5 points to a wetter-than-normal winter for **San Francisco**, while WMO warns of drought in southern Africa and the Amazon.

sections.heading: El Niño Reaches Very Strong Category as WMO Forecasts December Peak
sections.body:
El Niño has crossed into the "very strong" category. The relative anomaly in the central Pacific reached +2.0°C for August through October, according to an analysis by Meteored based on the criteria used by the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. The warming is not finished yet. The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) projects that sea surface temperatures in the tropical Pacific may rise to 3.8°C above average from November 2026 to January 2027, with the peak expected in December.

"This is literally off the monitoring charts that we have used for the past four decades," WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo said. She added that El Niño "will peak towards the end of 2026 but its impacts will be felt long after that".

sections.heading: Two Ways to Measure
sections.body:
The +2.0°C figure comes from NOAA's Relative Oceanic Niño Index (RONI), which NOAA began using in February 2026. The index removes background warming across the tropical oceans. Under the older Oceanic Niño Index, the event had already reached very strong levels in July through September, at +2.2°C, and rose to +2.5°C for August through October. The WMO's 3.8°C projection uses the conventional anomaly. Meteored estimates it could equal roughly +3.2°C to +3.4°C on the relative scale.

NOAA's Climate Prediction Center says a strong-to-very-strong El Niño is likely through January–March 2027. It also puts a 70% chance on a historic event for November–January, meaning one stronger than any since 1950. A WMO regional update warned of drier months across much of the western Pacific and said there is "a high chance" this will be the strongest El Niño on record since 1950.

sections.heading: A Wet Signal for California
sections.body:
California's outlook is wet. All 51 runs of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts' seasonal model, released November 5, call for a wetter-than-normal December through March around San Francisco, the San Francisco Chronicle reported. The average forecast is about 26 inches of rain, nearly double normal. January is expected to be the wettest month, with more than 8 inches.

Unusually warm coastal water adds to the risk. The model expects ocean temperatures off California to peak 10 to 13 degrees Fahrenheit above normal in December. That would put water near San Francisco close to 67 degrees instead of the usual 54. Warmer water can give incoming storms more moisture.

NOAA's winter outlook also favors wetter-than-average conditions across the southern US, from California to Florida, and a warmer-than-average northern tier.

sections.heading: Global Contrasts
sections.body: Elsewhere, the WMO outlook points to drier conditions in southern Africa, rainfall shortfalls in Southeast Asia and a higher drought risk in Central America and the Amazon. Saulo said a powerful El Niño "does not have to be a recipe for humanitarian disaster," and called for "decisive action, especially to protect the most vulnerable communities."

title: Google executive Don Harrison quits SpaceX board
summary: Harrison, a director since Google's 2015 investment, left as independent directors weigh a possible SpaceX-Tesla merger. The filing cites no disagreement.
bullets:
- **Donald Harrison**, a **Google** executive, resigned from **SpaceX**'s board effective immediately and cited no disagreement with the company, according to a filing disclosed Friday.
- Harrison joined the board in 2015 as part of Google's investment, and Alphabet remains SpaceX's largest institutional investor, according to CNBC Versant Media Group, Inc..
- He leaves as special committees at SpaceX and **Tesla** Tesla, Inc. study a possible merger, which **Elon Musk** says is not guaranteed.

sections.heading: Google executive Donald Harrison resigns from SpaceX board
sections.body:
Donald Harrison, a longtime Google executive, has resigned from SpaceX's board of directors with immediate effect, according to an 8-K filing the company submitted Friday. He had served on the board for more than a decade. His departure comes while independent directors are studying a possible merger with Tesla.

The filing says Harrison, a Class B director, told the company on Wednesday, Nov. 4, that he intended to resign. It adds that his "decision to resign was not due to any disagreement with the Company on any matter relating to its operations, policies, or practices". SpaceX thanked him for "his many contributions and his years of dedicated and outstanding service." The filing does not name a successor.

sections.heading: A decade-long Google tie
sections.body:
Harrison has worked at Google since 2005 and is its president of global partnerships and corporate development, CNBC reported. He joined SpaceX's board in 2015 as part of Google's investment in the company. He was considered an independent director, Bloomberg Law reported. The Information put that investment at nearly $1 billion.

The two companies remain closely linked. According to CNBC, Alphabet is SpaceX's largest institutional investor, with a stake worth $74 billion as of Friday's close. Google has also agreed to pay SpaceX's AI division up to $920 million a month for computing capacity from data centers near Memphis. "While Don is stepping down from the board, we remain deeply supportive of SpaceX's mission and are excited to continue our long-standing partnership," Google said in a statement to CNBC.

sections.heading: Merger talks in the background
sections.body:
Harrison is leaving as SpaceX's board considers a possible merger with Tesla, the electric vehicle maker also run by Elon Musk, The Wall Street Journal reported. On SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call on Oct. 20, Musk said both companies had set up special committees of independent directors to study a combination. He added that he is not part of those discussions because he is a conflicted party.

Musk said no terms had been agreed and that a deal was not guaranteed. He also pointed to a hurdle on Tesla's side: approval would require "a 50 percent vote of all shares, not just those who vote, but of all shareholders". Barclays analysts estimate that if SpaceX bought Tesla, Musk would own about 37% of the combined company but hold about 56% of its voting power, Reuters reported.

Neither the filing nor Google says whether Harrison was on SpaceX's special committee or whether Google will keep a seat on the board. SpaceX went public about five months ago in the largest IPO on record, according to CNBC. Tesla's annual shareholder meeting is set for Dec. 3.

title: Meta's Muse AI agent can now build custom app-like spaces
summary: Users describe an idea in chat, like a gift tracker or word game, and Muse builds an editable, interactive version.
bullets:
- **Meta** launched spaces Friday, letting **Muse** users turn chat descriptions into app-like trackers, planners and games, available wherever Muse operates.
- Connected third-party apps keep spaces updated automatically, and users can pin, hide or schedule spaces, according to Meta.
- The launch follows Thursday's Muse Voice debut; **Mark Zuckerberg** said in October the agents reached 10 million U.S. and Canadian users, TechCrunch reported.

sections.heading: Meta Launches Spaces, Custom App-Like Tools Built by Muse
sections.body:
Meta on Friday, November 6, introduced spaces, a feature that lets users of its Muse AI agent describe an idea in chat and have Muse build an interactive, app-like experience inside the Muse app. In its announcement, the company said a space can be "a holiday gift tracker, a daily word game, or a planning board for your next DIY project." Spaces are available starting Friday everywhere Muse is available.

It is the second new Muse feature in two days, as Meta keeps adding to an agent product it launched only a few months ago.

sections.heading: How spaces work
sections.body:
"Describe an idea in chat, and Muse builds a space for you, whether that's a tracker, a planner or a project board," Meta said, according to TechCrunch. The Verge reported that other examples include a shopping hub, a school dashboard, a music tracker and a trivia game. After a space is created, users can keep changing it by asking Muse, and they can check off items, add notes and make edits directly inside it.

Spaces can also connect to third-party apps. "Connect the apps you use, and your spaces keep themselves up to date in the background, so new concert dates, price changes, or savings progress show up without you having to ask," Meta said. Users can pin spaces to the sidebar, move them into the main tabs, hide them, or schedule when they appear. Meta's example is keeping a weekly planner up front during the workweek and switching to weekend plans on Saturday, The Verge noted.

Alongside spaces, Meta is rolling out a "specialized" version of its Muse Wonder AI model. The company also said it is looking at ways for users to share spaces and work on them together, according to The Verge.

sections.heading: Zuckerberg's own spaces
sections.body: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg promoted the feature in a post on X: "Playing around with spaces in Muse lately — tell Muse what you need and it builds it. I've made a BBQ game, an event tracker, and a home control dashboard. Excited to see what you build," TechCrunch reported.

sections.heading: A quick run of updates
sections.body:
On Thursday, November 5, Meta announced Muse Voice, which lets users video chat with their agent and give it spoken commands, TechCrunch reported. On Meta's October earnings call, Zuckerberg said the agents had 10 million users in the U.S. and Canada less than two months after they launched.

Muse is up against other AI agents with cartoon-like personas, including OpenAI's dots and SpaceXAI's Grokbot, according to TechCrunch.

title: IBM unveils first Illinois quantum computer in Chicago
summary: Housed at UChicago's Hyde Park Labs, the IBM Quantum System Two will anchor Illinois' National Quantum Algorithm Center before moving to IQMP.
bullets:
- **IBM** International Business Machines Corporation unveiled an IBM Quantum System Two at the **University of Chicago**'s Hyde Park Labs on Friday and calls it its most advanced system.
- The machine runs IBM's **Nighthawk r2** processor, which has 120 qubits according to IBM. Cloud customers can already use it under the name "ibm_chicago".
- It will later move to the **IQMP** campus on Chicago's South Side, where Illinois has committed $500 million, the Chicago Tribune reported.

sections.heading: IBM unveils first Illinois quantum computer in Chicago
sections.body: IBM unveiled its first quantum computer in Illinois on Friday, November 6, an IBM Quantum System Two at the University of Chicago's Hyde Park Labs. The company describes it as its most advanced system available. IBM unveiled it together with the University of Chicago, the State of Illinois and the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park (IQMP), and the machine runs on IBM Quantum Nighthawk, the most powerful quantum chip IBM has built, according to IBM. The system will anchor the state's National Quantum Algorithm Center. It will later move to the IQMP campus going up on the former U.S. Steel site on Chicago's South Side, the Chicago Tribune reported.

sections.heading: A public-facing machine
sections.body:
The computer uses the Nighthawk r2 processor. It sits at street level behind floor-to-ceiling windows on 53rd Street, IBM's quantum blog said. IQMP CEO Harley Johnson called it "probably the most publicly visible quantum computer in the world." IBM lists Nighthawk r2 with 120 programmable qubits and up to 25 times the speed of the previous generation, according to its hardware page. Cloud customers on Premium, Flex and Pay-As-You-Go plans can already use the new processor under the name "ibm_chicago," IBM's service changelog shows.

"I want the next generation of breakthroughs to happen in Illinois and the jobs and opportunity that come with them to benefit the people of Illinois," Governor JB Pritzker said in the release. IBM CEO Arvind Krishna said the system "can deliver scientifically useful results to organizations across the state of Illinois and beyond."

sections.heading: Building a quantum hub
sections.body:
Pritzker set up the algorithm center in 2024, with IBM as a leading member. Its Grand Challenge participants include Deloitte and AbbVie, which are working with IBM and Northwestern University on molecular simulation for drug discovery, IBM said. Separately, EPRI and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign are studying quantum optimization for power grids.

System Two machines already run in New York, Japan and Spain, the Tribune noted. The state has committed $500 million to the quantum park, including $200 million for a shared cryogenic plant. PsiQuantum is also building at the site. In April, IBM announced its FutureNow Chicago center at the park and said it would create 750 jobs. The center will be an anchor tenant in the Quantum Works building, which is expected to be finished by 2028.

sections.heading: Research momentum
sections.body:
Earlier this year, a team from the University of Chicago and IBM showed quantum advantage on a structured computing task. The experiment used 70 logical qubits and finished in about 15 minutes, IBM's blog said. UChicago Vice President of Research Nadya Mason said, "For our graduate students, having access to a quantum computer is incredible."

IBM will hold its Quantum Developer Conference in Chicago from November 11 to 13, according to its events page.

title: Anthropic IPO buyers weigh $1.1 trillion after AI rout
summary: Prospective investors now discuss $1.2 trillion to $1.3 trillion, down from $1.5 trillion, after a post-election tech selloff, Bloomberg reports.
bullets:
- Prospective **Anthropic** IPO investors are discussing a $1.2 trillion to $1.3 trillion valuation, and some are considering $1.1 trillion, Bloomberg reported Friday.
- The **Nasdaq 100** lost a record amount of market value Thursday after a Democratic midterm sweep raised fears of curbs on data center expansion.
- Investors have floated a smaller raise or a delay, according to The Wall Street Journal News Corp, and Reuters Thomson Reuters Corporation reports doubts about a November listing.

sections.heading: Anthropic IPO valuation talks fall to $1.2 trillion after AI selloff
sections.body: Prospective investors in Anthropic's initial public offering are now discussing a valuation of $1.2 trillion to $1.3 trillion, and some are considering a figure as low as $1.1 trillion, Bloomberg reported on Friday. The talks follow a sharp selloff in AI stocks after the midterm elections. The new range is a steep drop from the $1.4 trillion to $1.5 trillion buyers had recently told bankers, and from estimates as high as $2 trillion in early October, according to Bloomberg's reporting. People familiar with the matter said no final decisions have been made. Anthropic declined to comment.

sections.heading: Investors push back
sections.body:
On Thursday, The Wall Street Journal reported that three major investors planning to take part in the offering expected the valuation to come down, with one putting it closer to $1 trillion. Anthropic has been aiming to list the week before Thanksgiving and was expected to raise up to $100 billion. Investors floated two alternatives, a smaller raise or a delay. The Journal said Anthropic executives and advisers are expected to meet in the next few days to discuss the plans.

Reuters reported that potential buyers doubt the roadshow, planned for the week of November 9, can go ahead in time for a November listing. Some see $1.5 trillion as the high end of expectations. Investors are also waiting for Anthropic's October revenue figure, which the company left blank in its updated S-1 filing.

sections.heading: A market rout
sections.body: The Nasdaq 100 fell 6.4% on Thursday and lost a record $2.3 trillion in market value in a single day, while the Cboe Volatility Index hit its highest level since April 2025, Bloomberg noted. Investors were reacting to a Democratic sweep that raised the prospect of tighter limits on data center expansion. CNN reported that Anthropic recently disclosed nearly $900 billion in commitments for computing power and data centers. CNN also said odds on Kalshi of a November IPO dropped from above 90% to 60%.

sections.heading: Lower price or delay
sections.body:
Some analysts expect the deal to go ahead at a lower price. "My view is that Anthropic can still come to market and will come to market [but] will likely be forced to do so at a lower valuation," Mike O'Rourke of JonesTrading told CNN. Max Kettner of HSBC said a valuation around $1 trillion could reduce the risk of volatility once trading begins. Morningstar strategist Michael Field argued that a delay could do more damage. He said the company would likely "get it done at a slightly lower valuation, suck it up and move on," according to Bloomberg.

The valuation also matters for Anthropic's position against OpenAI. Anthropic raised private funding at $965 billion in May, and OpenAI has since taken in $11 billion at $1.25 trillion, the Journal reported.

title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Now Runs at 60 FPS on PC Emulators Lichii and Eglantine, a Day After Booting at 20-30 FPS - Wccftech
summary: The Nintendo Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time already runs at 60 frames per second on various PC emulators.
text:
Yesterday we reported that The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake was booting on PC at 15 to 30 FPS within hours of its official Switch 2 launch, albeit with heavy visual glitches. Just a day later, the situation has already massively improved.

DSOGaming reports that the Lichii emulator has fixed most of the remake’s visual issues in a single day, with the starting area and the Great Deku Tree now running at 60 FPS rather than the 20-30 FPS of launch day. One user on X went further, describing the latest build as running at a stable 4K 60 FPS with clear visuals , no bloom problem, no artifacts, and no slow motion, with only minor stutters and freezing left.

Separately, a Discord user running a 5700X CPU and RTX 5070 GPU with precompiled shaders reported in the Eglantine server reaching the Kokiri Sword from a new save with texture flickering still present on foliage and ground, a lighting fault on the Great Deku Tree during the opening animation, desynced audio in parts of the first cinematic, and slowdowns from low framerate. Which is roughly where you'd expect a two-day-old compatibility effort to be . Still, their video demonstrates a largely playable game, as you can see in the embed below.

The Eglantine repository shows the frantic activity of the modding team to improve Ocarina of Time compatibility. Lichii is a fork of Eglantine, which itself builds on Eden, yuzu and Sudachi, and Eglantine has pushed two Ocarina-specific test branches in the past day alone .

text:
Apple plans to merge the iPhone's Action button with the Camera Control starting next year, according to the leaker known as " Instant Digital ."

In a new post on Weibo, the leaker claimed that a single press of the combined button would open the camera, while a long press would trigger the function assigned to the Action button. They explicitly clarified that the dedicated Action button would disappear, while the Camera Control button would remain.

The proposed arrangement seems plausible given how the two features already work. The Action button predates the Camera Control and requires a long press to activate its assigned function, while a single press of the Camera Control opens the camera. Combining them in the way described would therefore preserve both familiar interactions, with the customizable action simply moving to a different location on the device.

A long press of Camera Control currently opens Visual Intelligence , but that feature has since been integrated directly into the Camera app as Siri mode in iOS 27 . That integration could give Apple room to reassign the gesture while keeping Visual Intelligence accessible through the Camera app.

It is notable that the iPhone Duo also lacks an Action button , despite retaining Camera Control. Its omission provides a precedent for an iPhone without the separate control and could hint at a broader change in the future.

text:
Add TechSpot Serving tech enthusiasts for over 25 years. TechSpot means tech analysis and advice you can trust . Looking Back: Sony's original MDR-3L2 headphones are a key part of the nostalgia surrounding the company's iconic TPS-L2 Walkman. As interest in wired headphones grows among teens, Sony has revived the MDR-3, combining a retro design with modern features, though at something of a premium over comparable on-ear models.

The new MDR-3R looks almost identical to the 3L2 that shipped with the first Walkman . Rather than sacrifice modern functionality for nostalgia, though, Sony swapped the 3.5mm plug for USB-C and added an inline remote and microphone for easy playback controls and hands-free calls.

In an age when the choice is usually between earbuds and large, ear-covering headphones, Sony says the MDR-3R is the lightest on-ear headset in its current lineup, weighing just 38g without the cable (which, at 1.2 meters, is noticeably shorter than the original's).

Sony also recreated the original packaging and manual and included removable orange and blue foam earpads. The 23mm drivers are unchanged too, so the sound should be close to the original.

text:

While some cool new features added to the video-sharing platform more recently optimized the user experience with features like conversational search and On-the-go mode, others, like when YouTube made users' TV experience worse on purpose via unskippable ads, show the company isn't completely tuned in to what people enjoy and loathe about its interface.

It seems the latest alteration to the app's navigation bar warrants several thumbs down – that is, if users can find the dislike button . In November 2026, YouTube unveiled a new navigation bar design that noticeably omits the "Subscriptions" option. The button, labeled "Subs," unassumingly hides on the top menu between the Home and Movies & TV options. Needless to say, some users were annoyed to discover the tab was no longer in its usual location.

"Who on earth decided that this is good design?" one Reddit user asked. The "Library" tab is also noticeably missing in action. Users now must navigate to their profiles to be able to view recent videos, downloads, playlists, and other selections usually found in their libraries. On top of moving these buttons to another location, users also observed that YouTube gave the navigation bar a liquid glass finish and a floating presentation.
